description: The plot illustrates how two accuracy measures (“Initial Accuracy” and “Final Accuracy”) vary as a function of “pop frequency (x10^4).” The x-axis is labeled “pop frequency (x10^4)” on a linear scale, spanning approximately 1 to 19 with regularly spaced tick labels every 2 units (1, 3, 5, …, 19). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick labels at 0.2 intervals (0.0, 0.2, …, 1.0). One line is green with square markers and a solid style (with vertical error bars), starting near 0.38 at x=1, rising to about 0.46 at x=3 and about 0.63 at x=5, dipping to around 0.50 at x=7, then increasing through roughly 0.56 (x=9), ~0.74 (x=11), and ~0.88 (x=13), followed by values around ~0.82 (x=15), ~0.83 (x=17), and ending near ~0.93 at x=19. The other line is blue with circular markers and a dashed style (also with vertical error bars), beginning around 0.68 at x=1, increasing to about 0.88 at x=3 and ~0.98 at x=5, dipping slightly to ~0.92 at x=7, rising to ~1.12 at x=9, dropping to ~1.00 at x=11, then increasing to ~1.02 at x=13 and ~1.22 at x=15, dipping slightly to ~1.18 at x=17, and ending near ~1.28 at x=19.
